key_insight: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces (DART) treats failed math solutions as starting points for finding better reasoning paths. Instead of relying only on independent attempts, it identifies uncertain steps and generates distinct alternatives.
problem_solved: For hard math problems, independent Monte Carlo sampling may rarely produce solutions whose final answers pass a verifier, limiting the accepted reasoning traces available for LLM post-training.
method: Start with a rejected reasoning trace and split it into individual reasoning steps.
Rank steps using position-weighted uncertainty to identify candidates for alternative reasoning.
Generate deliberately distinct alternatives; the supplied abstract is truncated before further procedural details.
impact: DART could help practitioners obtain useful training traces from difficult problems by reusing failed attempts. The supplied excerpt does not include results, so efficiency or accuracy gains cannot be confirmed.

paper_authors: Lukas Aichberger, Adam Golinski, Arno Blaas, Arwen Bradley, Jacob Springer
